hunt.label: Help-verb and inte hunt
hunt.title: Find inte and the four help verbs the page marks.

spots.rule: Inte (not) comes straight after the first verb: kan inte, vill inte, vet inte. In the command Oroa dig inte, it comes after oroa dig.
Kan (can) is a help verb. The next verb is an infinitive: kan läsa, kan sova. Kan du …? asks for help politely.
Vill (want to) is a help verb: vill sova.
Måste (must, have to) is a help verb: måste klara, måste sova, måste jobba.
Ska is a help verb too: vad jag ska göra = what I should do.

sections.title: Three verb forms: now, command, dictionary
body: A verb is a doing word. Today you need three verb forms. The present tense says what happens now or regularly. It ends in r: talar, köper, bor. The help verbs kan, vill, ska and måste are the exceptions. Swedish uses the same form for I study and I am studying: Jag pluggar. Never say Jag är pluggar.

The imperative (command form) tells someone to do something: Tala! Köp! Ring! Your teacher calls it the naked verb. The infinitive is the dictionary form. It follows a help verb and usually ends in a: tala, köpa, ringa. Dictionaries often show it with att (to): att tala = to speak.

Make the forms from the present tense, in three groups. Ar verbs: take away r. Talar becomes Tala! and tala; the command and the infinitive look the same. Er verbs: take away er for the command, then add a for the infinitive. Köper becomes Köp! and köpa. Short verbs: take away r. Bor becomes Bo! and bo; this infinitive does not end in a (also må).
Two verbs need extra care. Vara (be) is irregular: är in the present and Var! as a command. Kommer keeps only one m in the command: Kom! The infinitive is komma.

examples.fi: Jag talar svenska. · Tala svenska! · Jag kan tala svenska.
examples.en: I speak Swedish. · Speak Swedish! · I can speak Swedish.

examples.en: I feel well. · Be well! · I want to feel better.

examples.fi: Han kommer hem. · Kom hem! · Han måste komma hem.
examples.en: He is coming home. · Come home! · He has to come home.
examples.note: Kommer keeps only one m in the command: Kom!

examples.fi: Jag är glad. · Var glad! · Jag vill vara glad.
examples.en: I am happy. · Be happy! · I want to be happy.
examples.note: Vara is irregular: är in the present, Var! as a command.

items.why: Talar ends in r: it says what she does.
No r and no help verb: it tells someone to act.

Köper ends in r: present tense.
Köper loses er: Köp! is the command.
After vill, the verb ends in a: köpa.
Ringer loses er: Ring! is the command.
After måste, use the infinitive ringa.
Var! is the command of vara (be).

sections.title: Help verbs open the door to an infinitive
body: Kan (can), vill (want to), måste (must, have to) and ska (will, be going to) are help verbs. The verb after them is always the infinitive: kan tala, vill köpa, måste jobba, ska träna. Never use the present tense there: kan tala, not kan talar.
Hinner (have time to) and orkar (have the energy to) work the same way: Jag hinner gå till affären. Jag orkar inte plugga.
Two useful questions. Kan du …? asks for help politely: Kan du hjälpa mig? Ska vi …? suggests a plan: Ska vi dricka kaffe? To want a thing, say vill ha: Jag vill ha kaffe, not Jag vill kaffe.

examples.fi: Jag kan sjunga, men jag kan inte dansa.
examples.en: I can sing, but I cannot dance.
examples.note: Both verbs after kan are infinitives.

examples.fi: Jag vill ha kaffe.
examples.en: I want coffee.
examples.note: Use vill ha for wanting a thing.

examples.fi: I morgon ska jag träffa Elin.
examples.en: Tomorrow I’m going to meet Elin.
examples.note: Ska marks a plan; träffa is the infinitive.

examples.fi: Jag hinner gå till affären.
examples.en: I have time to go to the shop.
examples.note: Hinner is about time.

examples.fi: Kan du hjälpa mig?
examples.en: Can you help me?
examples.note: Kan du …? is a polite request.

examples.fi: Ska vi dricka kaffe?
examples.en: Shall we have coffee?
examples.note: Ska vi …? suggests a plan.

sections.title: Inte comes after the first verb
body: Inte means not. It makes a sentence negative. Put inte straight after the first verb. One verb: Jag simmar inte. With a help verb: Jag kan inte simma. Kan is the first verb, so inte comes before the infinitive simma.

English adds do: I do not swim. Swedish never adds an extra verb. The rule works with every help verb: Jag vill inte ha kaffe. Jag hinner inte komma. In a command, inte also follows the verb: Läs inte mer! Oroa dig inte!
Short adverbs such as ofta (often), alltid (always) and aldrig (never) go in the same place as inte: Jag dricker ofta kaffe. Jag dricker aldrig vin.
Finland-Swedish note: in fast speech in Helsinki you will often hear int instead of inte. Recognise it, but write inte.

sections.title: The verb stays second
body: The golden rule of Swedish word order is verb second (V2): in a statement, the first verb is always the second building block. Position one can be the person (Min mamma bakar en kaka i dag), a time (I dag bakar min mamma en kaka) or a place (I Finland dricker vi mycket kaffe).

The subject always stands right next to the verb: just before it or just after it. When a time or a place comes first, the subject moves to just after the verb. Count chunks, not words: I dag is one chunk in position one.
With a help verb and inte: I morgon ska jag inte jobba. Ska is in position two, then jag, then inte, then the infinitive. Questions with a question word follow the same rule: Varför kommer du sent?

examples.fi: Min mamma bakar en kaka i dag.
examples.en: My mother is baking a cake today.
examples.note: Subject first, verb second.

examples.fi: I dag bakar min mamma en kaka.
examples.en: Today my mother is baking a cake.
examples.note: Time first, then the verb, then the subject.

examples.fi: I Finland dricker vi mycket kaffe varje dag.
examples.en: In Finland we drink a lot of coffee every day.
examples.note: Place first, dricker second.

examples.fi: Varför kommer du sent?
examples.en: Why are you late?
examples.note: The question word is position one; kommer is position two.

RETURN: Tomorrow, say a kan line, a måste line and a negative line without looking.
assignment.model: Jag kan tala engelska. Jag kan laga mat. Jag kan simma. Jag vill träna. I morgon måste jag plugga svenska. Jag jobbar inte på fredag.

takeaways: Present tense usually ends in r; the command is the naked verb; the infinitive is the dictionary form that follows a help verb.
After kan, vill, måste and ska, use the infinitive: Jag kan tala.
Put inte after the first verb: Jag kan inte komma. In a command too: Oroa dig inte!
A time phrase may come first, but the verb stays second: I dag bakar min mamma en kaka.
